title: A single sub that fails alignment aborts the entire Stack & Share run and deletes the partial result, even though the code counts 'rejected' frames as a normal outcome
summary: Closed by an earlier wave and independently re-verified here, not taken on trust. packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/stack_and_share_service.dart:400-432 wraps the follower `_addStackFrame` await in a try/catch that increments framesProcessed/framesRejected, records the reason into `rejectionReasons`, emits progress and CONTINUES; only a loss of provider authority (`if (!_hasAuthority) rethrow;` at :415) still propagates to the run-level catch. :435-446 additionally treats an Ok whose stackedFrameCount did not advance as a rejection. :459-466 fails the run ONLY when nothing but the reference survived (StackAndShareAllFramesRejectedException naming the dominant reason) rather than persisting a one-sub 'stack'. The finding's 'expected' also asks for the rejected count in the completion state: the dialog shows 'frame X/Y, Z rejected' live (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/stack_result/stack_and_share_dialog.dart:722-723) and on completion navigates to the result screen, which renders 'Frames stacked', 'Rejected' and an 'Attempted' pill (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/stack_result/stack_result_screen.dart:510-541), with StackAndShareResult.framesRejected = framesAttempted - framesStacked (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/imaging/stack_and_share_models.dart:512-514).
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/stack_and_share_service_test.dart — 'a rejected follower is counted and skipped; the run continues' and 'a run whose followers are ALL rejected fails with the dominant reason instead of persisting a one-frame "stack"'. 23/23 green.
revert_check: Re-reverted this wave, not quoted from the earlier one: inserted `rethrow;` as the first statement of the catch at stack_and_share_service.dart:415 (restoring the pre-fix behaviour where a native Err escapes the follower loop). Both tests failed (+21 -2). Removing the rethrow restored 23/23.

title: Settings search is a raw substring match, so any two-word phrase a user would actually type ('capture folder') returns 'No settings match your search'
summary: Closed by an earlier wave at the caller the verifier's correction named, and re-verified here. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/settings_screen.dart:172-181 splits the query on whitespace and requires EVERY token to match — `tokens.every((token) => sectionMatchesToken(section, token))` at :178. sectionMatchesToken (:43-50) falls through to kSettingsSearchSynonyms (:30-40), which carries the app's own vocabulary for files-storage ('capture folder', 'capture directory', 'save path', 'image folder', 'disk space', 'free space', 'storage location'), so bare 'disk' matches as a substring of 'disk space'. SettingsSectionDef.matches (settings_catalog.dart:80-89) correctly stays a single-token predicate — tokenisation belongs to the caller. Confirmed there is exactly one search surface: nothing outside settings_screen.dart / settings_catalog.dart / settings_search_index.g.dart references SettingsSectionDef or kSettingsSearchTerms.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/settings_search_query_test.dart — 'a two-word phrase finds the page that owns the setting' now also covers the finding's third literal repro, bare 'disk' (it previously covered only 'disk space'). 7/7 green.
revert_check: Replaced settings_screen.dart:178 with the pre-fix `if (section.matches(query)) {`. 'a two-word phrase finds the page that owns the setting' failed. Restored: 7/7 pass.
caveats: settings_search_index.g.dart was regenerated (`dart run tools/production/settings_search_index_gen.dart`) because --check reported it stale. It was ALREADY stale before this batch — the diff carries row-title changes from concurrent work in connection_settings.dart / location_settings.dart / image_grading_settings.dart, not only the new 'Backups' row title. The generator is not wired into any melos or CI gate. Its self-test has one check failing, 'resolves labels past a closed nested call', which asserts the index contains 'Global minimum exposure (s)' — that string exists nowhere in packages/skotiq_app/lib and was absent from the index before the regeneration too, so it is a stale assertion from an earlier rename, not a regression from this work.

title: The Share Card's metadata strip is clipped: it renders 'M51  Integration 00:35:00  Frames 7  Fil…' and the filter is cut off the right edge
summary: The reported input was already closed by an earlier wave (share_card_renderer.dart:323-350 fitCaption walks the arial48/24/14 ladder down from the height-derived font and greedy-wraps whole 'LABEL value' segments until each fits the card width minus padding), but the SAME defect still shipped for a wider caption: when no ladder entry fits, fitCaption returned the smallest font with the segments UNCHANGED and handed them to img.drawString, which slices at the card edge. Measured, not assumed: a 115-char target name on a 512 px card needs 746 px against 496 px available at arial14, and a rendered PNG had luminance-255 glyph pixels throughout the right-hand padding. fitCaption now ellipsizes any segment that still does not fit at the smallest font (share_card_renderer.dart:347-355 + the new _ellipsize at :357-379), using ASCII dots because the built-in bitmap fonts have no U+2026 glyph and a missing glyph is silently dropped — which would leave a shortened caption carrying no mark that anything was removed. Checked the other call sites: stack_result_screen.dart:852 and live_stacking_broadcast_service.dart:494 are the only production ShareCardSpec builders and both use ShareCardLayout.bottomBar, so both go through this path; cornerCard has no production constructor.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/share_card_renderer_test.dart — new 'a title too wide for the smallest font is ellipsized, not sliced by the card edge' renders the PNG and scans the caption band's right padding for bright pixels (plus asserts the segment ends with '...' and measures inside the bar). Existing 'no glyph is drawn in the right-hand padding of a 512px card' and 'every wrapped row measures within the card width, losing nothing' still cover the originally-reported input. 28/28 green.
revert_check: Two severances. (1) New fix: replaced `_ellipsize(smallest, segment, available)` with `segment` in fitCaption's fallback comprehension — the new test failed (+27 -1); restored, 28/28. (2) Pre-existing fix: replaced `final fitted = fitCaption(font, segments, bitmap.width); final barFont = fitted.font; final rows = fitted.rows;` in _drawBottomBar with `barFont = font; rows = [segments];` — 'no glyph is drawn in the right-hand padding of a 512px card' failed; restored, 28/28.

title: Automatic backups are ON by default and write to ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups, a location the Files & Storage page never names and offers no way to change
summary: Two of the three halves were already closed and are cited rather than re-fixed: the PATH half (backup_service.dart:1065-1078 _getBackupDirectory resolves through resolveDefaultBackupDirectory at :130-139, which follows the resolved database file and therefore honours SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR) and the DISCLOSURE half (file_path_settings.dart's _BackupFolderRow names the resolved folder and states the retention policy). The half the earlier wave explicitly caveated as unbuilt — 'offers no way to change it' — is what this fix closes, because that is the half the finding's 'expected' is about: an observatory PC's system volume is routinely the smallest on the machine and the default folder follows the database onto it. BackupService gains `backupDirectorySettingKey` ('backup.directory'), `getConfiguredBackupDirectory()` and `setBackupDirectory(String?)`; _getBackupDirectory consults the setting before the default, so ALL consumers move together — createBackup, autoSaveBackup, listBackups (which is what retention prunes from), the headless backup/filesystem handlers and sync_service all go through that one method. setBackupDirectory creates the folder eagerly so an unmounted or read-only volume fails at the picker rather than at 3am. The key is stripped from _exportSettings (:751-758) and skipped on import (backup_service/sequence_codec.dart:20-25) so restoring a bundle cannot repoint where THIS install writes and deletes. UI: the Backups row gains 'Change…' (directory picker → setBackupDirectory → both providers invalidated so the row re-reads the service) and, once a folder has been chosen, 'Use default'; the row's retention sentence stops claiming 'beside the database' once the folder is somewhere else.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/backup_directory_setting_test.dart (new, 7 tests) drives a real BackupService built exactly as backupServiceProvider builds it (no injected directory provider): a chosen folder is where createBackup/autoSaveBackup/listBackups actually land, the folder is created eagerly, an uncreatable path throws, clearing stops writing to the old folder, blank means default, the bundle does not carry the key, and restoring a bundle that DOES carry it cannot move the folder. packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/file_path_backup_folder_test.dart gains 5 tests: the picker's result reaches the writer, cancelling writes nothing, a moved folder is no longer described as 'beside the database', 'Use default' sends null, and the default state offers no reset. 7/7 and 9/9 green.
revert_check: Three severances. (1) Removed the `final configured = await getConfiguredBackupDirectory(); if (configured != null) return Directory(configured);` lines from _getBackupDirectory — 'a chosen folder is where backups are actually written' and 'clearing the choice stops writing to the old folder' failed (+5 -2); restored, 7/7. (2) Deleted `await _move(context, ref, picked);` from the Change… button's onPressed — 'the folder can be moved from the page' failed; restored. (3) Replaced the Use-default button's `onPressed: () => _move(context, ref, null)` with a no-op — 'a moved folder can be handed back to the default' failed; restored, 9/9.
caveats: The row is inside the `if (!isRemoteMode)` Application Data section, so a remote client still cannot move the imaging host's backup folder — the same scope the other infra paths (sequences/database/logs) already have. Existing bundles are not migrated when the folder moves; the comment on setBackupDirectory says why (silently relocating an archive is not what the operator asked for). Pre-existing failures observed while running the surrounding suites, none of them from this batch: packages/skotiq_core test/services/import/nina_sequence_fidelity_test.dart fails 6 tests with 'Wait Has No Time Set', introduced by WaitTimeUnconfiguredRule in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/timing_rules.dart (mtime 2026-08-03 23:16, hours before this session) against a NINA fixture whose Wait node has no time; and packages/skotiq_app test/screens/settings/captures_landscape_test.dart fails 2 host-baseline golden pixel diffs, which dart_test.yaml documents as excluded from `melos run test` via --exclude-tags golden. With goldens excluded, all 414 tests under packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings pass.
